methodology: Whole-session known-policy attacks. First half sessions profile; second half are held out. Public variants use public per-epoch features. Policy-interval variants additionally derive conservative hidden-arrival intervals from public capacity transitions, public policy parameters and the sampler noise support; they do not replay or infer the noise draw. For os_csprng, known-seed replay is skipped because the public experiment seed does not determine the OS-CSPRNG noise stream. Labels are used for profile training and target scoring only.
limitations: The OS-CSPRNG transcript cannot be replayed from the public seed. Interval features are conservative deterministic transforms of public counts, not additional observations or an optimal likelihood attack; capacity censoring can make them uninformative. Its sampler has a conditional approximate-DP bound under independent uniform bits, but this analysis is not an independent implementation audit. Failure to classify does not establish privacy. The naive arm is the leaky positive control. The experiment excludes latency, sampler timing/CPU, errors, billing, network and runtime observations.
